decisions.reason: As a newly launched, highly strategic automation product that fits the firm's publicly stated direction and likely required substantial engineering investment, management would be inclined to continue with it and treat any weak early response as temporary.

Because this robot extends the firm's established automation offering and was publicly introduced only recently, management would tend to justify the investment by keeping it on the market unless clear failure had already become undeniable.

Although more niche than the core shuttering robots, it still builds on the firm's broad integrated precast solution set, so the firm is likely to persist with it after recent development and market introduction.

This product is closely aligned with the firm's automation roadmap and existing capabilities, and given the recent launch and visible commitment, management would more likely keep it than admit the rollout was premature.
